title: Positive-degree natural comparison for the underlying Zariski abelian sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For every pair of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules $F,G$ [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], suppose $m(F,G,\varphi):F_{et}\to G_{et}$ is an abelian sheaf morphism of the associated tensor-sections sheaves [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], with component $\Gamma(U,u^*\varphi)$ at every etale object $u:U\to X$. Let $F_{ab}$ be the underlying abelian sheaf of $F$ on the small Zariski site. For all such $F$ and all $n\in\mathbb N$, there exist simultaneously additive equivalences $e_F^n:H^{n+1}(X_{Zar},F_{ab})\simeq H^{n+1}(X_{et},F_{et})$ [def-sc-zariski-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], natural in every module map: $e_G^n\circ H^{n+1}(\varphi_{ab})=H^{n+1}(m(F,G,\varphi))\circ e_F^n$. The Zariski groups may be computed by the small Ext model from enough injectives and the etale groups by the standard large Ext model. No degree-zero assertion or module-category derived-sections comparison is made.

proof.text: Use the inclusion of open subschemes into the etale site. For each open W, identify the underlying abelian sections of F on W with tensor-pullback sections along W into X by the unit-normalized comparison of left adjoints between module restriction and tensor pullback. The restriction composition unit equation makes these identifications compatible with inclusions of opens. Naturality of the left-adjoint comparison in F makes the direct image of the specified m(F,G,phi) equal to the underlying abelian sheaf map of phi. This constructs the natural direct-image identification.

proof.text: Evaluate an injective resolution of the associated etale sheaf at an affine open object W. Cohomology over that object is the global cohomology of its localization on the small etale site of W. Tensor-pullback composition identifies the localized sheaf with the tensor-sections sheaf of F restricted to W. Quasi-coherent affine acyclicity makes this group zero in every positive degree. When working with large coefficients, the coefficient-lift resolution comparison identifies the same complexes before and after lifting, so this applies to the original coefficient universe as well. Every open is covered by affine opens; hence all positive object-cohomology sections are locally zero. Sheafification is zero and the sheafified-presheaf description gives zero positive higher direct images.

proof.text: The Leray edge map, namely site-cohomology pullback followed by cohomology of the counit, is invertible by positive higher-direct-image vanishing. Compose with cohomology of the direct-image identification from step 1. The two sides are computed from the same evaluated resolutions: Ext via an injective resolution identifies the small enough-injectives Zariski Ext model and the standard large etale Ext model with the resolution computations. The canonical resolution maps, independent of choices by homotopy, preserve additivity and naturality. Composing the naturality squares of step 1, site-cohomology pullback, and the counit yields the asserted equality for phi. Only positive degrees are asserted; no comparison of module-category derived sections or degree-zero normalization is part of this statement.

theorem etaleZariskiAbelianPositiveComparison (X : Scheme.{u})
    (m : ∀ (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent],
      (F ⟶ G) → (etaleTensorSectionsSheaf F ⟶ etaleTensorSectionsSheaf G))
    (hm : ∀ (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
      (φ : F ⟶ G) (U : X.Etale),
      (m F G φ).hom.app (op U) = ((tensorPullback U.hom).map φ).app ⊤) :
    letI : EnoughInjectives
        (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :=
      @IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives _ _ _
        (Sheaf.isGrothendieckAbelian_of_essentiallySmall'.{u}
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    letI : HasExt.{u}
        (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :=
      hasExt_of_enoughInjectives _
    ∃ e : ∀ (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (n : ℕ),
        (Sheaf.H' ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj F)
          (n + 1) (⊤ : X.Opens)) ≃+
        @Sheaf.H _ _ X.smallEtaleTopology (etaleTensorSectionsSheaf F)
          inferInstance (HasExt.standard _) (n + 1),
      ∀ (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
        (φ : F ⟶ G) (n : ℕ)
        (x : Sheaf.H'
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj F)
          (n + 1) (⊤ : X.Opens)),
        e G n (((Sheaf.cohomologyPresheafFunctor
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) (n + 1)).map
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).map φ)).app (op ⊤) x) =
        @Sheaf.H.map _ _ X.smallEtaleTopology inferInstance (HasExt.standard _)
          _ _ (m F G φ) (n + 1) (e F n x)
